correctness.rationale: PASS: For c≥3 and n≥0, direct summation of floor(cj/2)+1 for 0≤j≤2n proves P_c(2cn)=c n²+(floor(c/2)+2)n+1, including odd c. With d_c=floor(c/2)+2, the positive Pell unit u²-abv²=1 gives integral T=[[u,av],[bv,u]] with determinant 1 and Tᵀ diag(b,-a)T=diag(b,-a). A positive power is identity modulo 2ab because T is in a finite invertible matrix group, so its positive orbit through (d_a,d_b) recovers positive integers n,m. Norm invariance expands exactly to a n²+d_a n=b m²+d_b m, and the orbit strictly grows: infinitely many positive equal-count partition pairs. Exceptional parameter pairs with ab square are ≤H/2 times the harmonic sum, yielding O(H log H), hence density one. The standalone pure-integer verifier directly checked 684 polynomial sections, 87 nonsquare Pell parameter pairs and the 169 equality example; these finite tests support, not replace, the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: PASS: Conjecture 4.6 proposes infinitely many equal restricted-partition values for every a<b. The theorem proves it for all nonsquare-product pairs, a density-one family with only O(H log H) exceptional parameter pairs up to H. It provides a uniform explicit infinite-family mechanism, covering all odd/even parity combinations not reached by the earlier both-multiples-of-four theorem. The remaining square-product locus is mathematically specified and nontrivial, so the work is not a renaming or an isolated numerical example.
